ranking_quote: 5,P0003,Hexagonal self-avoiding-walk scaling limit,attempted_un,SAW to SLE(8/3): field-defining conjecture
current_open_status: UNKNOWN: original source posed it as open in 2022; no exhaustive current solved/retired check completed
exact_source_statement: Grimmett Question 2.2 asks whether a uniformly distributed n-step self-avoiding walk from the origin of the hexagonal lattice converges weakly, after a suitable rescaling, to an SLE(8/3) random curve. The source does not specify the rescaling, curve topology, or SLE variant.
primary_source: G. R. Grimmett, Selected problems in probability theory, arXiv:2205.07318v1 (2022), Question 2.2, printed p. 3, https://arxiv.org/html/2205.07318, lines 89-93; PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.07318, lines 88-94
primary_quote_short: Does a uniformly distributed n-step SAW from the origin of H converge weakly, when suitably rescaled
related_source: H. Duminil-Copin and S. Smirnov, Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012), Conjecture 1, https://www.unige.ch/~smirnov/papers/saw-j.pdf, printed p. 1662: critical-fugacity chordal boundary-to-boundary honeycomb SAW to SLE(8/3).
important_distinction: The original P0003 fixed-length free-endpoint ensemble is not the related critical length-weighted boundary-to-boundary ensemble; no transfer theorem has been verified.
source_fidelity_note: Grimmett's line preceding Question 2.2 appears to print kappa(H)=sqrt(1+sqrt(2)), but the cited Duminil-Copin-Smirnov Theorem 1 proves sqrt(2+sqrt(2)); do not copy the typo into a theorem card.
